notes: Non-test code is essentially identical to the reference; tests cover Placeholders() extraction, request-only expressions (upstream.host, escaped literal, similar-prefix name) and direct ph() response retries by parametrizing the existing status-code test.

Non-test code matches the reference fix exactly; tests parametrize the existing status-code retry test over shorthand and direct ph() and add unit and end-to-end request-only cases for every scenario the maintainers listed.

Works and folds constant string concatenations, but it hardcodes reverse-proxy placeholder names (including meaningless `rp.*` raw names) inside the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher, which is a layering smell, though the tests are thorough (GET/POST, transport-error restriction, dynamic names).

Works and even folds constant string concatenations, but it puts reverse_proxy placeholder knowledge, including unneeded rp.* aliases, into the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher, which is a layering smell; the tests are solid and include a real transport-error restriction case.

Correct, with a predicate-based ReferencesPlaceholders API, but the AST walk is inlined in Provision, the test duplicates isResponsePlaceholder, and the latency test relies on time.Sleep, so it is slightly timing-dependent.

Correct AST-based detection exposed through a predicate API, plus an accurate update to the struct doc comment; tests are very thorough, though the sleep-based latency cases are slowish and the transport-error test uses a dial error, which is always retried anyway, so it proves little.

Sound design with Placeholders() returning names plus a dynamic flag and the predicate kept in reverseproxy; very thorough unit and integration tests covering every maintainer-specified edge case and direct ph() retries, with only a reasonable doc-comment refresh beyond the fix.
Equivalent to the reference, with Placeholders() returning names and a dynamic flag and a doc comment update; very thorough unit, matcher-set and end-to-end tests, including a direct ph() retry test.

Clean use of ast.MatchDescendants/FunctionMatcher to collect literal names and a dynamic flag, a minimal reverseproxy predicate, and solid table plus integration tests that also verify the upstream receives the body once.

Walks the checked AST to record ph() names, sets a dynamic flag for non-literal names, and keeps the reverse-proxy-specific placeholder list in reverseproxy; the accessor returns the internal slice instead of a copy, and the tests are good but cover only one request-only case end to end.

Correctly collects literal and dynamic ph() names at provision time and keeps the response-placeholder list in reverseproxy through a clean predicate API, with a good table test plus an end-to-end POST regression test.

A concise predicate-based API with a dynamic flag and the response placeholder list kept in reverseproxy; a broad matcher-set table covering escaped literals, prefix look-alikes, comprehensions and dynamic names, plus one end-to-end regression test.

Covers all diff commands plus the stash pipe and fixes the parser, but the helper mutates args directly instead of using Config. It also adds a speculative pathFromRenameLine special case for custom-patch trees, which adds complexity the task didn't call for.

Parser fix is sound and adds a heuristic that strips the tree directory from rename-to lines in custom-patch diffs. StandardDiffPrefixes prepends to self.args by hand instead of using Config(), overrides mnemonicPrefix, and the extra pathFromRenameLine/separator machinery adds complexity beyond the spec.

Matches the reference design closely: it overrides noprefix and src/dstPrefix but leaves mnemonicPrefix. It folds the overrides into AddCommonDiffArgs, so stash show and the worktree diff are covered automatically, though this is slightly implicit. Parser changes mirror the reference.

Closest to the reference: it forces noprefix/srcPrefix/dstPrefix but leaves mnemonicPrefix alone, and it reads rename/copy-to paths unquoted and unstripped. Folding the prefix config into AddCommonDiffArgs covers stash show and the worktree diff automatically, at the cost of touching every AddCommonDiffArgs caller; added tests are mostly command-arg updates.

The parser fix is sound: it strips any single-component prefix, prefers rename/copy-to paths, and splits the diff --git line on matching halves; the --src-prefix/--dst-prefix CLI args also work for diff/show. However, it never covers `git stash show`, so with diff.noprefix the new stricter parser now mis-resolves stash diff paths, and that call site is one the task explicitly required.

Parser changes match the spec and come with thorough unit tests plus an integration test, using --src-prefix/--dst-prefix args instead of config. It leaves stash show without forced prefixes, so with diff.noprefix the new strip-first-component parser now mis-resolves stash diff paths, a case the reference covers.

A config-based helper forces a/ and b/ on every diff command, including stash show and the `stash show -p | git apply -R` pipe (beyond the reference but in the task's spirit), and the parser matches the reference semantics. It overrides mnemonicPrefix rather than leaving it alone, and the visible test changes are mostly arg-expectation churn.

Fixes the parser (any single-component prefix, rename/copy-to lines, no-prefix resolves to empty) and forces a/ b/ through config on every diff command, including stash show and the SaveStagedChanges pipe into git apply. It also forces diff.mnemonicPrefix=false, which overrides the user's mnemonic prefixes in displayed diffs where the reference keeps them; tests are mostly updated command-arg expectations.

Uses an alternative design that asks the circular exemplar storage at GC time, so protection survives restarts automatically, and it releases chunks and the appender correctly. However, it takes the global exemplar lock and serializes labels for every GC candidate while holding the stripe and series locks. It depends on buffer contents rather than accepted exemplars, offers no protection before commit, and uses variadic optional-parameter hacks. The tests cover only head truncation and the selected-series path.

Querying the circular exemplar storage by labels during GC works and covers WAL replay and snapshot restore for free, but it ties head GC to the storage through a type assertion and an extra lock, uses hacky variadic optional predicates, gives no protection before commit, and its tests skip stale compaction, AppenderV2 and snapshots.

Tracks exemplar timestamps at append time as the reference does, plus during replay and snapshot restore, and releases chunks correctly in gcSeries. The ordinary gc path does not clear the appender, which likely explains the hidden-test failure. The variadic optional-parameter hack on gc and gcSeries is unidiomatic, and the tests skip stale compaction, AppenderV2 and snapshot paths.

Closely follows the reference: it records timestamps at append time, on replay and on snapshot restore, and releases chunks in gcSeries, but it leaves series.app set in the ordinary gc path (retaining the removed chunk's appender), relies on variadic cutoff parameters, and fails one hidden test.

Correctly tracks the latest exemplar timestamp on memSeries during commit, WAL replay and snapshot restore. It keeps the series in both gc paths, clears the appender and releases chunks with correct metrics and mmap-ready accounting. Recording at commit time instead of append time leaves a small race window. The state-bit packing shrinks the pending-commit mask, and the new head test detaches an existing test's doc comment, but the DB test covering all modes, both appenders and snapshots is excellent.

Correct and complete across Compact, selected and stale compaction, with appender release, chunk metrics and min-time handling, very thorough tests covering both appenders, snapshots and double restarts, and a compact state-flag design; drawbacks are commit-time rather than append-time recording and a new test inserted so that it steals an existing test's doc comment.

The core design is close to C1, but changing the stripeSeries.gc signature probably breaks compilation of existing callers and tests, which fits 0/3 hidden tests and the failed suite. The gc path also never clears series.app, so retained series keep a reference to the removed chunk. WAL-replay tracking runs even when exemplar storage is disabled.

Clean state-flag design with thorough restart tests, but it changes the stripeSeries.gc signature (which breaks the hidden tests' callers and fails the whole package), never clears the appender in the ordinary GC path, and only records exemplars at commit time.

Fixes the nested cancelling flow but is broad: done callers now bypass the IsDone guard, so a failed caller with no children gets overwritten to Cancelled, RefreshReusableCallerStatus gains an extra run refresh, and the run is settled and emitted on every cancel; it has only one model test.

The new cancelCaller does keep callers cancelling until their children settle, but done callers now bypass the IsDone early-return, so a failed or skipped caller with no children can be overwritten to Cancelled. It also adds a band-aid run refresh in RefreshReusableCallerStatus, always runs SettleRunAfterCancel, and always calls EmitJobsIfReadyByRun, which is broader than needed; only the nested model test was added, with no force-cancel/concurrency test.

A dedicated caller-cancel path writes Cancelling while any child is cancelling, which fixes nesting, and the tests are thorough end to end; it also unconditionally calls SettleRunAfterCancel, and rewriting a status the cascade already set can return 0 rows on MySQL, logging a spurious error.

Routes callers through a dedicated cancel that stays Cancelling while any direct child is cancelling, which works for nested callers and for force. It overwrites from a possibly stale in-memory row and also removes the settle early-return; the tests are the strongest, including single/nested ack and an end-to-end concurrency-waiter wake.

Keeps a caller cancelling when a direct child is cancelling by re-aggregating in cancelOneJob, and emits the run when it is done with no job updates; it works but passes a stale caller struct to RefreshReusableCallerStatus and always reports the reloaded row as updated even when nothing changed.

Compact fix: a caller with a cancelling child is re-aggregated instead of being force-set to Cancelled, plus the same done-run emit as the reference. The cancelling branch always returns the reloaded caller even when nothing changed, which can report spurious updates and skip settling; tests cover the nested ack and the waiter re-emit.

Closely mirrors the reference by reloading expanded callers after their children's cascade and comparing to the input status (only unexpanded callers go through cancelOneJob), plus a minimal concurrency emit; the service test checks the emit but not that the waiter actually wakes.

Closest to the reference: an expanded caller is reloaded after its children's cascade, re-aggregated if it is not done yet, and falls back to cancelOneJob when it has no children. The emit-on-done-run condition in cancelRun is sound, and there are focused tests for both the nested ack cascade and the force-cancel emit.

A sound master-fd refcount design with careful SetUnlinkOnClose ordering and an abstract-socket guard, but the broad internal refactor fails all hidden tests, and its tests use t.TempDir for socket paths, which can exceed sun_path limits.

A master-fd unixSocket redesign that looks functionally sound (no leaked dups, race-safe, handles '@' names and double close), but it changes the unixSockets map type and wrapper fields, which breaks every hidden test and the package suite.

A minimal fix close to the reference: it closes the duplicated file, uses a CAS closed flag, does a locked decrement/close/unlink with a stored path, and skips abstract sockets (no GOOS check); thorough tests cover sharing, double close, races and unixgram.

Fixes the root cause like the reference: it closes the leaked dup in reuseUnixSocket, does the refcount decrement, close and unlink under unixSocketsMu, uses a CAS closed flag that returns ErrClosed, stores the path and skips '@' names; the existing close-newest-first reuse issue remains (also present in the reference), and the tests are thorough and cover every requirement.

Fixes the fd leak and the refcount issues with a new master-fd unixSocket type, but the large refactor also changes listener.go, deleteListener semantics, listenerPool counting and adds a second mutex, which together break every hidden test.
Functionally plausible master-fd approach, but it adds a second mutex, changes listenerPool accounting for reused sockets, edits listeners.go and the delete wrappers, and breaks every hidden test.

A clean master-fd refcount redesign that unlinks under unixSocketsMu and checks GOOS for abstract sockets, but it changes internal types and deleteListener receivers well beyond the needed fix, and a second Close returns a wrapped OpError rather than net.ErrClosed itself.

Clean master-fd refcount design that also fixes reuse after the newest holder closes, with good race and abstract-socket tests, but it also rewrites deleteListener/deletePacketConn and the internal types, so the hidden test suite does not compile against it (0/7).

The wrapper and plugin changes essentially mirror the reference and are correct. However, it changes unrelated production code in mib_loader.go (gosmi AppendFS workaround plus a nil-logger default) to make an environmental test pass.

The wrapper and Gather changes closely match the reference and the tests are adequate. It also carries unrelated production changes: the gosmi AppendFS rewrite and a nil-logger fallback in LoadMibsFromPath.

The reconnect, engine reset and close-on-error logic is correct. However, it modifies mib_loader.go production code, with an unchecked type assertion and a redundant Name assignment, for an unrelated gosmi path issue, and its tests do not cover Get/Walk reconnecting a closed connection.

The core fix is correct and closes immediately on error, and it also clears ContextEngineID. It rewrites gosmi path loading in mib_loader.go, an unrelated production change with an unchecked type assertion, and it has no test for Get/Walk reconnecting.

Correct wrapper-level fix: Get and Walk reconnect a closed connection, Reconnect resets the SNMPv3 USM state and ContextEngineID, and the plugin closes the agent's connection on failure; tests are strong. The suite failure most likely comes from the pre-existing gosmi path issue in TestSnmpInitGosmi, which this candidate also edited out of scope, and calling s.Log.Debugf on every close risks a nil-Log panic in tests.

Clean reset helper that also clears ContextEngineID, immediate close on field and table errors, and strong wrapper and gather tests. closeConnection always calls s.Log, which panics in tests where Log is unset, and the gosmi test-path tweak is unrelated.

Over-engineered: it adds unexported fields to the exported GosnmpWrapper to restore configured engine values, which are toml:"-" and unused for inputs.snmp, and this breaks unkeyed struct literals, the likely cause of the hidden test failure. It also rewrites MIB loading in mib_loader.go, which is unrelated production code.

Adding private fields to the exported GosnmpWrapper breaks unkeyed literals (likely why a hidden test fails), and restoring configured engine values deviates from the required fresh discovery. It also adds a custom gosmi dirFS and an extra Init call in mib_loader.go, which the task did not need.

Clean fix that closely follows the reference; clearing the localized keys is redundant but harmless. Tests are thorough, covering v1/v2/v3 reconnect-on-request and verifying that a healthy agent's connection is left untouched. The only scope issue is the unrelated TestSnmpInitGosmi edit, which is also the likely cause of the environmental suite failure.

Close to the reference and closes immediately on error. Tests are thorough, covering v1/v2/v3 Get/Walk reconnects with a silent agent and checking that a healthy agent's connection is not closed; the only extra is an unrelated tweak to the gosmi test path.

The wrapper fix is correct and an excellent packet-level test confirms a fresh noAuth discovery after reconnect. The plugin defers the close to the end of the gather rather than closing right after each failure, so recovery only happens on the next interval. It also includes an unrelated TestSnmpInitGosmi edit.

Fixes the issue in the wrapper by resetting USM engine, key and context state when reconnecting a closed connection, and Get/Walk reconnect first. However, the deferred close means tables in the same gather keep using the stale session, and it also tweaks the unrelated TestSnmpInitGosmi; the package-suite failure looks environmental.

Reference-like implementation with correct suffix-aware NewObject and root handling, plus copy and hostile-escape tests that confirm the safety requirement holds without extra filtering; the zip Open past-end special-casing is a bit clunky and the squashfs test needs mksquashfs.

Mirrors the reference semantics, including root-at-symlink handling. The zip Open special-casing for symlink offsets past the end is clunky and partly redundant. Tests are strong, with an end-to-end copy test and a hostile-archive sentinel test.

Close to the reference for both backends, with NewObject and root-at-symlink lookups consistent with List and a sensible offset clamp; small quirks are calling Info() for every squashfs entry and treating a trailing-slash symlink as a file.

Close to the reference for both backends. It handles a root pointing at the suffixed link name and keeps NewObject consistent with List. The only extra is a harmless offset clamp applied to all zip objects. Tests are good, using a binary squashfs fixture.

Reads --links from the per-call ctx instead of at construction, so symlinks stay in the zip dirtree without --links and are only filtered in List/NewObject; it also hides members under a symlink even when --links is off and logs the notice on every List.

Zip symlinks always go into the dirtree and are filtered only at List/NewObject time using the request context. Members under symlinks are dropped even without --links. There is no construction-time links setting and the skip notice repeats on every listing, which makes the design fragile.

Reads --links from ctx in squashfs but at construction in zip, deletes members under or equal to a symlink name (diverging from the reference), and has a zip root-at-symlink bug that empties the listing without --links.

Reads the links config from the per-call context instead of at construction. In zip, the suffix is added after root matching, so a suffixed root fails, and an unsuffixed root at a symlink without --links yields an empty single-object Fs. It also hides members under symlinks rather than relying on existing protections.

Core behaviour works and passes hidden tests, but the zipRemote refactor counts out-of-root entries as 'escape the archive', a root only selects a symlink by its bare name rather than its .rclonelink name, squashfs lookup code is duplicated, and squashfs has no tests.

Symlink support works and adds clash protection, but the zipRemote refactor now counts entries outside the root as escaping the archive, which gives a misleading log. A root pointing at a symlink only works without the .rclonelink suffix, the reverse of how List names it. Tests cover zip only.

Over-engineered: it adds a shared case-insensitive LinkFilter to the archiver package that also drops regular .rclonelink members on clash, reads link targets eagerly, and rebuilds the whole squashfs directory on every NewObject; it fails a hidden test.

Adds a new shared LinkFilter with case-insensitive clash logic, which is overengineered. It can drop regular members ending in .rclonelink, contrary to the spec. The shared dirEntries does make List and NewObject agree, and the tests are extensive.

Covers both backends, root-at-symlink, duplicate symlinks and clashes, and has strong copy tests; however, it reads every link target eagerly when the zip is opened (one remote read per symlink at mount) and drops a symlink that has members under it, which differs from the reference and likely explains the hidden test failure.

The squashfs side is solid. The zip side reads every link target eagerly and silently drops any symlink that clashes with a directory or file. That is safe, but it changes what is exposed and is more complex than needed. Tests are thorough, including copy and clash cases.
